researcher_notes: Coverage is highly bimodal and split along a clear line: vendors that publish their own dedicated, dated customer case studies (Olo, ItsaCheckmate, Deliverect, Otter, ChowNow) came back with solid, verifiable evidence; vendors whose go-to-market model doesn't run through named case studies (DoorDash Storefront, Slice, Bbot, Cuboh) came back thin or empty despite extensive searching, and this appears to be a real characteristic of those vendors' businesses rather than a research gap. Olo (public, ticker OLO) was the strongest single vendor -- 6 dated, high-confidence case studies (Waffle House, Five Guys, Denny's, Cracker Barrel, Portillo's, Slim Chickens), all reused/re-verified against the 2026-07-21 archive's 48 indexed 'olo' candidate_evidence URLs plus fresh fetches for scope/date/metric confirmation; none of the fetched Olo case-study pages carry an on-page publish date, so dates cited are either explicit in-text statements (e.g. Waffle House's 'brand-wide across all locations in 2023') or, where absent, the record notes that no page-level date could be confirmed. ItsaCheckmate and Deliverect both came back strong with genuine enterprise deployments carrying explicit unit counts and clear dates (Wendy's 6,000+ locations 2022-09-28; Arby's/Inspire Brands 1,100+ units 2020-09-30; Papa John's all-US-restaurants phased rollout announced 2026-03-18; Little Caesars global 2024-01-17). Uber Direct / Uber Eats for Merchants produced exactly the kind of evidence the task asked to watch for: both records found (White Castle, McDonald's UK & Ireland) are explicitly white-label delivery-as-a-service integrations behind the brand's own app, not Uber Eats marketplace listings, and both press releases say so directly. Otter and ChowNow each produced a small but genuine bench of named multi-unit customers. Four vendors -- DoorDash Storefront, Grubhub for Restaurants, Slice, and Cuboh -- were the weak spots: DoorDash Storefront in particular is a notable gap given DoorDash's overall market position, but despite many search variations no DoorDash-published, dated, named-brand Storefront case study could be located (DoorDash does not appear to publish customer case studies for this product the way Olo/Otter/ItsaCheckmate do); the best available evidence is a third-party industry scan (Restaurantology.io, April 2025) citing '399 brands with 2+ locations' showing Storefront usage signals, which is aggregate and unnamed, so no record was created from it. A large share of DoorDash- and Grubhub-related search results were straightforward marketplace listing pages (doordash.com/store/..., individual restaurant Grubhub ordering pages) rather than technology-enablement announcements -- exactly the failure mode flagged in the task instructions -- and these were excluded throughout. CORPORATE STRUCTURE FINDINGS: (1) The task brief's assumption that Ordermark and Nextbite are a single merged company is OUTDATED/INCORRECT as of this research date: Ordermark rebranded to Nextbite in November 2021, but after a round of 2023 layoffs, Nextbite SOLD Ordermark's U.S. order-aggregation/tablet-consolidation business to India-based UrbanPiper in June 2023 (confirmed via PR Newswire and multiple trade press). Around the same time, Nextbite itself (the virtual-kitchen brand-licensing business) was acquired by SBE Hospitality/Sam Nazarian (announced June 12, 2023). So today these are two separate companies under two separate owners: 'Nextbite' (virtual brands, under sbe) and 'Ordermark' (order aggregation, under UrbanPiper) -- not a unified entity. Only one Nextbite record (Nathan's Famous, a virtual-brand licensing deal, 2023-04-19) is included; no Ordermark-branded evidence was found or attempted given this split. (2) Bbot was acquired by DoorDash (announced 2022-03-01, ~$88M); evidence indicates its technology was folded into DoorDash's Platform Services/in-store ordering and payments product suite rather than continuing to operate as a distinct customer-facing brand -- no dated, named restaurant-CHAIN customer evidence (as opposed to a single venue) was found either before or after the acquisition, so Bbot is recorded as thin/likely-absorbed. (3) Grubhub's sale by Just Eat Takeaway to Wonder Group closed January 7, 2025 ($650M), confirmed, followed by ~500 layoffs announced 2026-02-28 as part of integration -- consistent with the task brief. 'Grubhub for Restaurants' today appears to be simply the branding of Grubhub's restaurant-partner web portal (marketplace + Grubhub Direct + POS integrations) rather than a single named product with its own case-study library; the only usable record found was indirect (a POS-vendor integration press release naming a small franchise owner). (4) Cuboh was acquired by ChowNow, announced 2024-03-28 (Business Wire) -- confirmed, no corrections needed to that lineage, but no named-brand evidence exists for Cuboh under either owner. (5) Uber Direct and Uber Eats for Merchants are confirmed as the correct, current, distinct product names -- no renaming found.

vendors_with_thin_or_no_evidence: DoorDash Storefront -- despite extensive searching (product pages, press releases, trade press, industry-scan coverage), no DoorDash-published, dated, named-restaurant-brand case study or press release was located. DoorDash does not appear to publish dedicated customer case studies for Storefront the way Olo/Otter/ItsaCheckmate/Deliverect do for their products. The best available evidence is a third-party industry scan (Restaurantology.io, April 2025) reporting '399 brands with 2+ locations' show usage signals, and a Restaurant Dive article (2023-06-28) with only generic, unnamed restaurant references -- neither is a named, dated relationship, so no record was created. A quote attributed to a 'WNB Factory VP' about Storefront could not be traced to its original source article and was excluded rather than guessed at.

Grubhub for Restaurants -- only one usable record found (Flippin' Pizza, via a third-party POS vendor's press release, not a Grubhub-published case study), well below the 3-10 target. Most Grubhub-related search results were either marketplace listing pages or generic 'Grubhub Direct' marketing content aimed at independent restaurants rather than dated, named multi-unit chain relationships.

Slice -- Slice's business model specifically and almost exclusively targets independent, typically single-location pizzerias (its stated market differentiation vs. competitors); despite searching, no genuine multi-unit restaurant CHAIN customer with a name and date was found. The one dated program found (Slice Accelerate, a $15,000 tech-grant program for 100 independent pizzerias) does not name individual qualifying pizzerias with multi-unit scope.

Bbot -- no dated, named restaurant-CHAIN customer evidence was found either before or after DoorDash's 2022 acquisition. The only named customer reference located (Brooklyn Barge, a single NYC bar/restaurant venue) is a single-location business, not a multi-unit chain, and carries no publish date. See vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_renamed for the acquisition/absorption finding.

Cuboh -- no dated, named restaurant-brand customer evidence was found under either its independent operation or its post-March-2024 ownership by ChowNow; only generic marketing copy and acquisition-announcement coverage were located.
vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_r: Ordermark / Nextbite -- the task brief's assumption that these are a single merged company is out of date. Ordermark rebranded to Nextbite in November 2021, but after 2023 layoffs, Nextbite SOLD Ordermark's U.S. order-aggregation/tablet-consolidation business to India-based UrbanPiper in June 2023 (PR Newswire, multiple trade press corroboration). Nextbite itself (the virtual-kitchen/delivery-only brand-licensing business) was separately acquired by SBE Hospitality/Sam Nazarian around the same time (announced 2023-06-12). As of this research date these are two separate companies under two separate owners -- 'Nextbite' (virtual brands, sbe-owned) and 'Ordermark' (order aggregation, UrbanPiper-owned) -- not a unified entity. Recommend Todd split these into two separate vendor lines going forward rather than one combined 'Ordermark/Nextbite' entry.

Bbot -- acquired by DoorDash (announced 2022-03-01, ~$88M). Evidence indicates Bbot's technology has been folded into DoorDash's Platform Services/in-store ordering and payments product suite rather than continuing to operate as a distinct, actively-marketed customer-facing brand; Bbot's CEO stayed on as a DoorDash digital product leader post-acquisition, but no new Bbot-branded customer announcements were found after the acquisition closed. Recommend treating 'Bbot' as a historical/absorbed brand rather than an entity likely to produce new dated evidence going forward.

Grubhub -- confirmed per the task brief: sold by Just Eat Takeaway to Wonder Group, deal completed 2025-01-07 for $650M, followed by an announced ~500-position layoff (2026-02-28) as part of integration. Not defunct, but under new ownership and mid-restructuring; 'Grubhub for Restaurants' branding appears to have consolidated into a general restaurant-partner portal rather than a single distinctly-marketed product line with its own case-study library.

Cuboh -- acquired by ChowNow, announced 2024-03-28 (Business Wire); Cuboh's online-ordering/POS-consolidation product is being folded into ChowNow's broader suite (ChowNow Pro, Order Better Network, Flex Delivery) per ChowNow's own acquisition announcement. Recommend treating 'Cuboh' as an absorbed/legacy brand going forward.
